newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo shares fall after earnings release.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo shares fall after earnings release.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc's share price fell more than three percent after the company reported disappointing 1996 fourth quarter earnings and lagging volume in its international beverage operations.
PepsiCo said its on-going operations earned $0.24 a share in the fourth quarter, down from $0.35 a year earlier.
International beverage volume was off nine percent, far more than analysts -- already braced for lower international beverage volume -- had anticipated.
Pepsico shares were off 7/8 at 33-1/4 at midday after touching a low of 33 earlier.
According to First Call, the company had been expected to earn $0.32 a share in the fourth quarter.
Analysts said PepsiCo's shares would be even weaker if the company's international beverage operations were not in such dire shape already.
"There's no place for the international beverage operations to go but up," said Terry Bivens, an analyst at Donald & Co. "That's why the stock isn't getting massacred."
PepsiCo's international beverage operations lost $404 million for the quarter, compared with a loss of $3 million a year earlier.
Bivens called the figures "a disaster" and said the depth of the international operations' losses was "greater than what most analysts were looking for."
He said the company had much to do to improve the business.

Last month PepsiCo said it would spin off its $11 billion restaurant operations and focus on its core beverage and salty snacks businesses. A major part of that focus will be international beverages, PepsiCo Chief Financial Officer Karl von der Heyden told Reuters in an interview after the announcement. He did not give details.

Analysts said today that PepsiCo was still unclear as to the changes it needs to make to its international beverage operations, and that even when the company does make changes, it will be some time before this business becomes profitable.
Martin Romm, an analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, said he did not expect the international beverage operations to post a profit in 1997.
Due largely to the woes of this business, Romm cut his 1997 earnings estimate for PepsiCo to $1.45 per share from $1.48.
"It's like climbing out of a very, very deep hole," he said of the company's efforts to improve its international beverage operations.
